rows.rationale: A has a refined editorial serif and good dark/cream section rhythm, but its entrance flashes the full headline at 80 ms, blanks it at ~500 ms, then re-types it, and the desktop hero leaves the right half empty; every hover crop is a flat lime field with no visible control or feedback. B builds from a clean blank into a staggered headline plus a live ledger panel, then uses scroll-linked storytelling (the 'One call. Four guarantees' stepper advancing between frames, a logo marquee, metric cards, charts, SOC 2 highlight, pricing slider). B's hovers show clear underline and button glow states, and both phone layouts are clean, so B reads as the more complete, award-calibre product page.

A has the bolder hero (a giant 'Ha lo' wordmark split by the glowing speaker) and more expressive hover feedback with a cursor follower and cream-to-amber fills, but it hides everything behind a 0-100 counter preloader for more than 2 s. On the phone the first viewport is still that loader, and a later materials card renders as a blank grey block. B's entrance choreographs the speaker and the line-masked headline into a finished hero by about 1.3 s. Its scroll scenes are just as varied (exploded view with callouts, sound-field diagram, tactile materials cards, glowing ring scene, staged delivery steps), and its mobile layout is clean throughout, which makes B the more consistently finished launch page.

A has the more distinctive art direction: a glowing moon over aurora wave lines, a staggered hero with floating phone callouts, and a sticky Listen/Adapt/Wake sequence whose sleep-stage chart changes with the time of night, ending on a warm sunrise download section. B is tasteful and editorial, with clean masked-headline entrances, a marquee, a sticky phone that changes screens, word-by-word text reveals, and teal and cream section shifts. Its near-black hero feels emptier and less memorable, though. B's hover states are clearer (animated underlines, outline brighten, CTA glow) than A's subtle pill and brighten effects. Both mobile layouts are clean.

Both are strong. A is restrained and editorial: a masked serif headline reveal, a word marquee, a sticky phone that steps through three stages, and a deliberate shift to green and cream sections. B has a richer cinematic hero with a glowing moon orb and animated wave lines, a staggered italic headline, and the phone rising with floating cards around it. B's sticky Listen/Adapt/Wake scene redraws a live hypnogram chart for each stage, and its feature, pricing and sunset closing sections are denser and more product-specific. Hover and mobile quality are about even, so B wins narrowly on visual richness and scroll-linked storytelling, though its purple palette is less original than A's.

A stages its hero with intent: the headline lines arrive in sequence, the timber-ring house shape rises in, and the nav settles by 2 s. Its scroll story builds the timber frame from plinth to skin, then moves into a horizontal project rail, stacked process cards and a big closing 'Norr' wordmark. B holds a counter preloader on a near-blank dark screen for about 2–3 s, and on mobile the first viewport is still stuck on '100/100' with no hero. Several of B's scroll frames catch half-revealed or clipped text, and its blurred custom-cursor disc covers button and link labels on hover, while A's underline and fill hovers are clean and legible.

A hides the whole first viewport behind a 0–100 counter preloader for about 3 s, and the mobile first viewport is still stuck on '100' with no hero. Several of A's scroll and mobile frames show half-revealed or clipped headlines ('Four places, built to be…', 'Quietly, and often'), and its blurry custom-cursor blob covers the button labels while hovering. B starts revealing its staggered hero by about 440 ms, with the wood-grain house shape growing in. Its scroll tells a real story (a timber hall built up plinth → frame → skin, then stacked process cards, an awards table and a giant 'Norr' sign-off), and it has clean colour-fill hover states and a solid phone layout.

A's entrance builds cleanly from an empty frame: the headline masks in line by line and the live-ledger code panel slides in beside it, so the hero settles by about 1.3 s with a real product visual. B shows its full headline at 80 ms, blanks it by 509 ms and then re-reveals it letter by letter, which reads as a flash of content. B's hero also leaves the right half empty. B's editorial serif type, stacked cream-and-dark panel transitions and big lime footer wordmark are striking, and its scroll story is as rich as A's (sticky stepper, metric cards, stacked testimonials, pricing). B's hover captures show only a lime surface with no visible control feedback, while A's nav underlines and glowing CTA hovers are clear; both phone layouts are clean.

B has the bolder art direction: a giant 'Ha lo' wordmark split by the speaker, a lit exploded view, a colour-swatch configurator and a custom cursor with fill-on-hover buttons. However, B's desktop shows only a counting preloader for about 2 s, and its phone first viewport is still stuck on the '100' loader, with an empty grey image card further down. A reveals its staggered masked headline and glowing speaker within about 1.3 s and keeps a clean, coherent story through the exploded parts, the sound diagram, materials, the 'ring of light' type moment and specs. Its mobile layout is consistently intact, though its hover feedback is modest.
